evals.prompt: We just onboarded a new LGU tenant. Create an OKF knowledge bundle under knowledge/tenant-system/ documenting the core entities: Organization, Tenant, and how tenant_id isolation works. Link the concepts together and include index files.
evals.expected_output: A conformant OKF bundle with frontmatter on every concept, root index.md with okf_version, subdirectory indexes, cross-links, and log.md initialization entry.
assertions: Root index.md exists at bundle root
Root index.md declares okf_version in frontmatter
Root log.md exists at bundle root
Root log.md has dated entry (YYYY-MM-DD)
Concept files exist for Organization and Tenant with non-empty type frontmatter
A concept or section documents tenant_id isolation
Cross-links use bundle-relative /path/concept.md format between related concepts
validate_okf.py exits 0 when run against the bundle
Concept bodies use terse prose: bullets over paragraphs, no filler words (just, basically, simply)

evals.prompt: Using the schema in .cursor/rules/project.mdc, add OKF concepts under a new knowledge/ bundle for the main PostgreSQL tables (tenants, admins, transactions). Use proper type names, # Schema sections, resource URIs, and bundle-relative links.
evals.expected_output: Concept files under a knowledge/ bundle with PostgreSQL Table types, # Schema tables, resource URIs pointing to schema sources, and updated index.md files.
assertions: Root index.md exists at bundle root
Root index.md declares okf_version in frontmatter
Root log.md exists at bundle root
Root log.md has dated entry (YYYY-MM-DD)
tables/index.md subdirectory index exists
Concept files for tenants, admins, and transactions exist with type PostgreSQL Table
Each table concept has a # Schema section with a markdown table
Frontmatter includes resource URIs pointing to schema source files
Tables cross-link to each other where foreign keys exist
Parent index lists all three table concepts
validate_okf.py exits 0 when run against the bundle
Concept bodies use terse prose: bullets over paragraphs, no filler words (just, basically, simply)

evals.prompt: Write an OKF playbook concept for incident response when a tenant sees cross-tenant data leakage. It should link to relevant auth/RBAC concepts and cite our module boundary rules.
evals.expected_output: A Playbook-type concept with Trigger and Steps sections, links to related concepts, Citations section, and log.md update entry.
assertions: Root index.md exists at bundle root
Root index.md declares okf_version in frontmatter
Root log.md exists at bundle root
Root log.md has dated entry (YYYY-MM-DD)
playbooks/index.md subdirectory index exists
A Playbook-type concept exists for cross-tenant data leakage incident response
Body includes Trigger and Steps sections
Links to at least two related auth/RBAC or isolation concepts
Citations section references module boundary rules or cursor rules
validate_okf.py exits 0 when run against the bundle
Playbook steps use terse format: bold verb labels, minimal filler

evals.prompt: How does tenant_id isolation work in this repo? Use the existing OKF bundle — run query_okf.py before reading concept files. Save answer.md (your answer), files_read.txt (one path per line, every file you opened), and query_log.txt (paste query_okf.py command + output).
evals.expected_output: Accurate isolation answer from 1-3 concepts max; query_log shows discover/query before bulk reads; files_read.txt lists at most 4 paths.
assertions: answer.md exists and mentions tenant_id isolation
query_log.txt exists and references query_okf.py or discover_okf.py
files_read.txt lists at most 4 file paths
files_read.txt includes tenant-id-isolation concept or query matched it
answer does not paste full bundle catalog
